acceptance_evidence: Public CLI tests prove doctor plus experiment init, run, resume, stop, and report behavior without model calls.
Fake Claude and Codex adapters drive reproducible task attempts through the existing stage and verify seam and produce immutable hashed artifacts.
Crash/resume and idempotency tests prove completed cells do not rerun and interrupted attempts are not counted as valid repetitions.
Budget, round, timeout, output, stop, redaction, and live-mode preflight gates fail closed.
Existing evaluator tests and the full relevant runtime suite pass, and documentation states the implementation and proof boundaries.
assumptions: This destination implements and verifies the zero-cost controller foundation; sealed private task authoring and credentialed live campaigns remain later authorized operations.
Append-only JSONL and immutable JSON/text artifacts remain sufficient; no database is introduced.
The accepted CLI and artifact-store seams satisfy the TDD seam-confirmation requirement.
Vendor adapters may be implemented and argv-tested without launching them; fake adapters are the only executable agents during verification.

constraints: Use test-driven vertical slices at the confirmed CLI and artifact-store seams.
Do not invoke Claude or Codex models, access enterprise credentials, spend quota, or modify global Claude/Codex files or hooks during local implementation verification.
Preserve every existing evaluator command and unrelated dirty-worktree change.
Use the Python standard library unless a later optional GEPA integration is isolated behind an absent optional dependency.
Real-model mode must fail closed until exact models, auth permission, usage cap, qualified isolation, and sealed-set configuration are supplied.
Commit, deployment, external publication, global configuration promotion, and Workbench closure remain unauthorized.
desired_outcome: A locally verified, zero-cost experiment controller can configure, initialize, dry-run, stop, resume, and report reproducible Claude Code versus Codex campaigns through fake adapters, while real model execution and global prompt or hook promotion remain fail-closed behind explicit authorization and safety gates.

facts.statement: The predecessor implementation plan passed artifact-validity review and fixes the CLI, adapter, state, safety, metric, and delivery contracts.
The existing package exposes argparse-based list, stage, verify, apply-reference, and validate commands with public-seam runtime tests.
The current implementation uses only the Python standard library and has no project-level dependency manifest.

rationale: The predecessor Workbench item produced and proved an implementation-ready plan. This successor implements that accepted design in the existing claude_harness_eval package, beginning with zero-cost fake-adapter and persistence slices so no account, credential, or spend decision blocks safe repository work.

assumptions: Live model use and global promotion will receive separate explicit authorization after local proof.
recommendation.choice: Implement the zero-cost controller foundation before any live campaign.
recommendation.rationale: Fake adapters and deterministic persistence exercise the highest-risk orchestration behavior without spending quota or exposing credentials, and preserve a clean gate for later live use.
tradeoffs: The first verified destination will not yet establish Claude-versus-Codex performance or install a winning global prompt.
